stance.label: US pullback deepens · DCA as planned

headline: SOX crashes 10.7%, Nvidia −14%; Nasdaq 100 is 0.2% from bear line, TSMC ADR −9.5%
summary: AI selling spread from Taiwan back to Wall Street: Friday was a panic crash in chips. By the rules, US stocks are still in a pullback, not a bear turn: credit, growth and jobs hold; valuations broke. All four US panic-bottom signals are on; Taiwan will face more pressure at Monday's open. SPY hit tier 2 today and QQQ is 0.1% from tier 4. Keep DCA as planned.

watch.label: S&P 500 200-day line

overview.lead: Friday was a panic crash in AI and chips: a reported accounting probe at Nvidia spread the selling across tech.
points: SOX −10.7%, every component fell.
Nasdaq 100 −5.6%, −19.8% from high, one step from a bear market.
Nvidia (NVDA) −14%; AMD (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO) and Micron (MU) all fell more than 12%.
S&P 500 fell 8.6% this week, its worst week since April 2025.
Equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) fell only 2% and is −7.1% from high: the selling is concentrated in big tech.

focus.lead: All nine fell; the three US tech names took the worst hit. QQQ nearly touched tier 4 and SPY newly hit tier 2.
points: QQQ −5.7%, only 0.1% from tier 4.
SPY −3.6%, −11.5% from high, past tier 2.
Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) NAV −7.5% on 11/20, −39.3% from high.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV −8.3% on 11/20, −43.5% from high, the deepest of the nine.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) and AB Select US Equity (LU0683600562) NAVs only run to 11/19 and miss Friday's Nvidia crash.
The two AB funds share 7 top-ten names, about 24% weight, including Nvidia and Microsoft; their next NAVs will fall together.
0050 and the Taiwan half of Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) will only price in the ADR crash at Monday's open.

position.lead: By the framework, SPY hit tier 2 today, using 25% of reserved cash in total; QQQ is 0.1% from tier 4.
points: SPY tier 3 at 662.23, 4.0% away.
QQQ has used 45% of reserved cash over three tiers; tier 4 is only 0.1% away.
AB Select US Equity tier 2 is 2.2% away (11/19 NAV).
AB International Technology tier 5 is 5.5% away (11/19 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used all tiers; further drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: The crash comes from AI valuations and company-specific doubts, not the economy: safe-haven money poured into Treasuries and yields fell.
points: 10-year Treasury yield 4.92%, down 0.21 point in a month.
Long Treasury ETF (TLT) rose 1.4%, one of the few gainers.
High-yield spread 3.52% (11/19), far from the 5% alarm line.
Fed Governor Cook said inflation pressure is spreading, but markets no longer fully price a 25 bp December hike.
Gold ETF (GLD) fell 3.7%; even gold being sold is a sign of deleveraging.
NT dollar 32.93 (11/19), 0.35 weaker in a month.

sentiment.lead: US fear has reached washout level: all four bottom signals are on, but panic alone does not mean the fall is over.
points: VIX rose to 35.89, higher than 97% of all days on record.
VIX term structure inverted at 1.16: short-term hedging demand far exceeds long-term.
CNN Fear & Greed 9.7, versus 37 a week ago.
S&P 500 RSI 25, oversold.
Only 4 of 11 sectors are above their 200-day lines.

sectors.lead: Only consumer staples closed up: money fled tech and chips for defensives and Treasuries.
points: Semiconductor ETF (SMH) −10.6%, −23.6% in a month.
Tech (XLK) −7.3%, software (IGV) −4.6%.
Consumer staples (XLP) +0.7%; health care (XLV) only −0.1%.
Anthropic (ANT) fell 8.5% on its second day, giving back most of its debut gain.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan must absorb another blow at Monday's open: TSMC ADR −9.5% and SOX −10%, though Taiwan already fell hard on Friday.
points: TSMC ADR (TSM) closed at US$318.71, still 5% above the Taiwan close after conversion.
UMC ADR (UMC) −10.2%.
632 margin accounts force-liquidated for NT$1.495B, both records (11/20).
Listed margin balance fell another NT$49.1B on 11/20, −32.5% in a month.
Foreign investors sold for 5 straight days, about NT$1.09T in a month.
Foreign net short in TAIEX futures 97,863 contracts, about 3,000 fewer in five days.

watch.lead: Monday: whether Taiwan holds above 0050's tier 5. US: whether the S&P 500 closes a 5th day below its 200-day line.
points: QQQ hits tier 4 with another 0.1% drop.
Nasdaq 100 closing below 24,980 means a bear market by definition.
Fewer limit-down stocks in Taiwan than Friday's 365 would signal forced selling is fading.
11/25 US PCE inflation; 11/26 US markets closed for Thanksgiving.
12/1 Jensen Huang's closed-door session with a US House committee.

regime.lead: By the rules, US stocks are still "pullback, but risk rising", not a bear turn: 2 of 7 systemic lights are on and the 200-day line still rises.
points: Trend: S&P 500 is 6.0% below its 200-day line for 4 closes, but the line is still rising.
Systemic lights: the index below its 200-day line and broad sector weakness are on; credit, growth and financial conditions show no problem.
Credit is closest to turning on, but the high-yield spread at 3.52% is still far from 5%.
Panic-bottom signals: all 4 on (oversold, VIX panic, inverted term structure, extreme fear).
History: of 43 drops to this level since 1929, 19 eventually went past −20%.
Of the 16 drops as fast as this one, only 6 went past −20%.
What flips it: 5 closes below the 200-day line at 7,349 with the line flattening → weak.
3+ systemic lights → may be turning bearish; below 6,255 → bear market by definition.
Taiwan stays "bear, risk rising" with 2 systemic lights on, not yet a full bear trend.
